composers_checked.name: Haydn, Joseph
composers_checked.note: 68 authentic quartets (Wikipedia list after Grove) all kept, plus the Seven Last Words (Op. 51), added from the gap check: IMSLP holds it only on the orchestral page, so the census missed it. Floor and durations from four complete cycles on MusicBrainz (Kodály, Angeles, Aeolian, Buchberger); minutes are their median. Op. 3 is Hoffstetter's (another slice).

note:
Haydn, string quartets and large strings: complete. Kept the 68 authentic quartets (Wikipedia list after Grove: Op. 1 Nos. 0-4 and 6, Op. 2 Nos. 1, 2, 4, 6, Op. 9 to Op. 103) and the Seven Last Words, Op. 51; floor and minutes from four complete cycles on MusicBrainz (Kodály/Naxos 8.502400, Angeles/Philips 464 650-2, Aeolian/Decca 478 1267, Buchberger/Brilliant 93889), minutes = median of their timings. Skipped as arrangements Op. 1 No. 5 (Symphony A without winds) and Op. 2 Nos. 3 and 5 (the cassations Hob. II:21-22 without horns); as doubtful the Echo, Hob. II:39 (no recording of the six-string original found), Hob. III:D3 and the Op. 12 print (Hob. III:Es4, A1); 24 collection and opus pages as duplicates of the single-quartet pages.
Where the brief was unclear, wrong or hard to follow:
(1) Benchmark imslpPage: the input matches the benchmarks to opus pages ("String Quartets, Op.64"), the brief's example uses the single page; I used the single pages, so the opus pages are skipped as duplicates.
(2) A gap work that IS on IMSLP: the quartet version of the Seven Last Words sits only on the orchestral page (Die Worte des Erlösers am Kreuze, Hob.XX:1) under arrangements, so the census missed it. The brief says gap additions get imslpPage null; I gave the IMSLP page and counted it as 0 added_not_on_imslp (the checker counts additions by null imslpPage). IMSLP's note doubts Haydn wrote or approved the quartet version; Wikipedia says he made it in 1787. Kept, under Haydn's name, as everyone performs it. Title without "(version for string quartet)" because Op. 51 / Hob. III:50-56 already name the scoring; that form is in aka.
(3) outOfScope reason looks wrong: the Cassations Hob. II:21 and II:22 (2 horns, 2 violins, viola, bass, one to a part) were left out as "string orchestra"; they are wind-and-string sextets and belong to c23 (winds-strings). Not added here (outside my formations); not checked for recordings.
(4) No Haydn slice covers string quintets: the Cassation in G, Hob. II:2 (strings, 1754, per the Wikipedia work list) may be a five-string work; not checked.
(5) Op. 103 is unfinished (two movements, about 11 minutes) but performed as it stands and in every cycle: kept with form "work"; the form definitions do not cover an incomplete multi-movement work.
(6) Years for Op. 1 and Op. 2 (and Op. 1 No. 0) follow benchmark 100010's "c. 1760"; IMSLP gives "ca. 1757-62" and Hob. II:6 "1765 or before".
(7) floor.published left blank everywhere: commercial recordings pass the floor and I opened no publisher pages.
(8) The notes come from movement headings (track lists, IMSLP) and standard facts; several are generic because Haydn's early sets are uniform. Levels are calibrated on the six benchmarks (early quartets 3, Op. 9 4, Op. 17-74 mostly 5, Tost works and late Op. 76/77 6); the graders should look hardest at Op. 17 (5) and Op. 54/55 (6).
(9) Technical: IMSLP's index.php?action=raw returns a compressed challenge page to scripts; api.php (prop=revisions) works and fetched all pages in four calls. MusicBrainz release lookups give whole box-set track lists with timings, which is the cheapest floor-and-duration source for a big composer; MusicBrainz does not allow recording browse by work with inc=releases.
(10) Op. 1 No. 0 is titled as a string quartet (as the cycles and Grove list it) with the IMSLP/Hoboken "Divertimento" name in aka. Violin entries 473 and 474 are duos for two violins: out of scope, not cross-listed. Op. 3 is catalogued under Hoffstetter (benchmark 100011), so it is left to that slice. No benchmark issues found (benchmark minutes fall within the cycles' timings).
